title: Fukushima Daiichi: tsunami design-basis exceedance, station blackout, and multi-unit severe accident
summary: Fukushima Daiichi is encoded as an external-hazard/design-basis and multi-unit severe-accident record. The first-pass grain is tsunami/external hazard, station blackout, loss of heat sink, emergency information, and post-event correction rails—not a complete Japanese legal, community, environmental, or energy-policy history.

place.location: Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant, Fukushima Prefecture, Japan

claims.claim: The NRC backgrounder describes the initiating event as a magnitude 9.0 earthquake followed by an estimated 45-foot / 14-metre tsunami; Fukushima Daiichi lost grid power, then many diesel generators, and Units 1–3 ultimately overheated, suffered core damage/melting, generated hydrogen, and experienced reactor-building explosions/releases.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: IAEA Technical Volume 1 says tsunami waves overwhelmed Fukushima Daiichi tsunami barriers, flooded primary and backup power systems and ultimate heat-sink systems, caused extended station blackout in Units 1–5, and left Units 1–3 unable to cope with extended loss of power and heat removal, leading to fuel overheating and melting.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The IAEA technical volume makes the design-basis/external-hazard issue explicit: the original tsunami design-basis height was OP +3.122 m, later re-evaluations included OP +5.7 m and OP +6.1 m, and the establishment permit did not consider combinations of tsunamis with other oceanographic events such as storm surges or high winds.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: The NRC response page records a correction surface after Fukushima, including orders for portable emergency equipment, spent-fuel-pool water-level monitoring, hardened/improved venting for applicable designs, and comprehensive earthquake/flooding hazard information.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: For the cube, Fukushima Daiichi is a design-basis humility record: a hazard envelope, common-mode external event, station blackout, heat-sink loss, and multi-unit emergency exceeded the assumed operating/control frame.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises this extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

evidence_profile.source_depth: one-pass NRC response page plus IAEA technical-volume extraction; Japanese primary reports deferred
limitations: Does not encode evacuation, decontamination, compensation, decommissioning, or public-health controversy in depth.

type_payload.system: boiling water reactor site / tsunami barriers / electrical power systems / ultimate heat sink / emergency response system
sequence_of_events: Earthquake caused off-site power loss and automatic shutdowns.
Tsunami exceeded site protection/design assumptions and damaged power/heat-sink systems.
Extended station blackout and loss of heat removal led to fuel overheating/melting in Units 1–3.
Hydrogen and releases produced building damage, contamination, relocation, and correction actions.
type_payload.proximate_cause: extended loss of power and heat removal after tsunami-induced flooding of critical systems
contributing_factors: severe-accident management and hazard re-evaluation gaps
latent_conditions: hazard-envelope assumptions were too narrow for the event realized
plant siting/layout made some critical systems vulnerable to common-mode flooding
correction rails were required after, rather than before, the stressor
correction_surfaces: post-event hazard re-evaluation and FLEX-like mitigation strategies in U.S. context

handling_notes: Preserve community harm and worker/family dignity; do not use nuclear accidents as spectacle.
Avoid reducing complex sociotechnical accidents to operator error or using records as blanket ideological claims about nuclear energy.

unknowns: Japanese Diet/NAIIC, government, TEPCO, and IAEA volumes 2–5 are not yet fully extracted.
No community displacement/recovery, decommissioning, dose, or food/water restriction child records are encoded.
International regulator-by-regulator follow-through remains future work.
